title.narrative: No Climate Justice without Land Justice - SECAM campaign COP27 2022 Egypt

description.narrative: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) Sixth Assessment Report (2021) indicates that it is unequivocal that human influence has warmed the atmosphere, ocean and land. Africa is the driest continent and is warming at twice the global rate. Before 1999, a drought happened once every five to six years in East Africa. Since 1999, they have been occurring every two to three years. Hunger already affects 240 million Africans daily. By 2050, warming of just 1.2 to 1.9- degrees, well within the range of current IPCC projections, is likely to increase the number of malnourished in Africa by 25 to 95 % – 25 % in central Africa, 50 % in east Africa, 85 % in southern Africa and 95 % in west Africa. Extractive industries have seamlessly interfaced with African governments, leadership class, governmental trade agencies, banks and investment firms, increasing pressure on the land. Africa's rangelands contain 36% of the world's total carbon and, if fully restored, can sequester carbon in amounts equal to that of the Amazon rainforest. But international interest in using African lands for carbon dioxide removal may present unique governance challenges concerning development trade-offs, land use rights, safeguarding of biodiversity and food security, and water resources. The Symposium of Episcopal Conferences of Africa and Madagascar - Justice, Peace and Development Commission (SECAM-JPDC) and its partners have given great importance to both COP26 and COP27, especially since the publication of Laudato Si by Pope Francis in which he states that climate is a common good for humanity. As a leading actor within the Our Land Is Our Life advocacy platform, SECAM proposes to lead a multi-actor campaign titled “No climate justice without land justice.”
